notes_729: iter729 — FIX-A reduce-to-whole-number direction canonical (iter728 = 4.5625 PASS; Q2 'round a dollar amount down' — responder's primary floor() answer was CORRECT but it volunteered a FALSE caveat: 'CAST(x AS integer) truncates toward zero (-47.89 -> -47)'). === STEP 1 GREP VERDICT = RESOURCE-DEFECT (not synthesis-slip). The false claim lived VERBATIM in the resource the responder cited (~r07:3665): 'for negative values prefer floor() because CAST(x AS integer) truncates **toward zero**, not toward negative infinity, per Trino math docs'. This is WRONG for Trino 467 — CAST(double/decimal AS integer) ROUNDS half-up, it does NOT truncate. (a) r07:3665 = the defect (Pattern C4a fixed-width-$N histogram section, the 'Equivalent CAST(... AS integer) form' note). (b) floor/ceil rounding content = r07 Pattern C4a (the floor(x/N)*N fixed-width bucket canonical, ~r07:3636-3673) + r07 §B2 round↔CAST (~r07:2355). (c) BEFORE iter729: truncate(x) was NOT documented as the toward-zero tool anywhere (only used in integer-DIVISION-truncation prose for / operator, not the scalar truncate() fn). (d) iter724 §4.4A DECIMAL inoculation (r27:1149/1175/1176/1192) + iter725 round↔CAST §B2 (r07:2355) CONFIRMED INTACT — preserved, NOT edited. === STEP 2 DOCS-VERIFIED (WebFetch trino.io/docs/467 math.html + conversion.html + language/types.html): (i) CAST(double/decimal AS integer) — conversion.html + types.html do NOT spell out the rounding rule (only general cast() text); CAST rounds half-up (CAST(47.89 AS integer)=48, CAST(-47.89 AS integer)=-48) is ESTABLISHED-stable-Trino-467 behavior, documented AS SUCH (not claimed verbatim-docs), consistent with iter726/iter728 conversion-page findings. (ii) truncate(x) VERBATIM math.html: 'Returns x rounded to integer by dropping digits after decimal point' = toward-zero/drop-the-fraction — CONFIRMED. (iii) floor(x) VERBATIM: 'Returns x rounded down to the nearest integer' = toward −inf — CONFIRMED. (iv) ceiling(x)/ceil(x) VERBATIM: 'Returns x rounded up to the nearest integer' = toward +inf; ceil = alias for ceiling — CONFIRMED. (v) round(x)/round(x,d) VERBATIM: 'Returns x rounded to the nearest integer' / 'rounded to d decimal places', '[same as input]' return type (half-up; rule not spelled verbatim but half-up is established) — CONFIRMED. === STEP 3 EDIT: (1) IN-PLACE FIX of the r07:3665 defect (reconcile, not append). BEFORE: 'for negative values prefer floor() because CAST(x AS integer) truncates **toward zero**, not toward negative infinity'. AFTER: rewrote the note to state CAST ROUNDS half-up (CAST(47.89 AS integer)=48, CAST(-47.89 AS integer)=-48; established Trino 467), so the CAST form does NOT give true bucket-floor semantics; prefer floor() for round-down, and use truncate(x) for toward-zero/drop-the-fraction. ALSO swapped the now-misleading CAST example block to use truncate(order_amount/50)*50 (the correct toward-zero/non-negative-floor tool) with an inline ❌-marked note that CAST rounds half-up and is NOT a floor. (2) ADDED a tight 4-way 'reduce a number to a whole number / drop the fraction' LEADING CANONICAL (anchor id reduce-to-a-whole-number) immediately AFTER the CAST example block, adjacent to the floor()/Pattern-C4a content: keyword anchors (round down to whole number, chop the decimals, drop the fraction, truncate decimals Trino, floor vs truncate vs cast, does CAST round or truncate, round to nearest integer, remove decimal places without rounding); 5-row direction table — floor(x)=toward −inf [47.89→47, -47.89→-48] ✅round DOWN; ceil/ceiling(x)=toward +inf [47.1→48] ✅round UP; truncate(x)=toward zero, DROPS fraction [47.89→47, -47.89→-47] ✅CHOP; CAST(x AS integer)=ROUNDS half-up [47.89→48, 47.4→47, -47.89→-48] ✅nearest int (NOT a truncate!); round(x,d)=half-up to d places same type ✅N places; two worked SQL examples (floor=round-down dollars, truncate=chop cents);
